questions.stem: What will be the Simple Interest earned on a principal sum of ₹8000 at an interest rate of 5% per annum over a period of 2 years?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT:
The formula for Simple Interest is SI = (P × R × T) / 100.
Here, Principal (P) = 8000, Rate (R) = 5%, and Time (T) = 2 years.
SI = (8000 × 5 × 2) / 100
SI = 80000 / 100 = 800.
Therefore, the simple interest earned is ₹800.
DECOY BUSTING: Note that ₹8800 is the total AMOUNT (Principal + Interest) at the end of 2 years. The question specifically asked only for the Simple Interest.
EXAM INSIGHT: Simple Interest remains constant every year because it is always calculated on the original principal. Compound Interest grows exponentially because it is calculated on the accumulated amount.
